infra-context

Bunkai infra map

How Bunkai TMS is built, run and deployed, and the budgets it must hold. Reverse-engineered from the target repo ../upex-bunkai-tms (paths below are relative to it unless they start with this QA repo's own folders).

Overview

Bunkai is a single Next.js 15 App Router monolith organised by feature folders: route handlers live under app/api/v1/<resource> and their logic under lib/<feature>/. Most business rules run inside Postgres as bunkai_* RPC functions guarded by Row Level Security, so the app layer is thin and the database is fat. There is no separate backend repository.

Deployment shape: the app runs serverless on Vercel (vercel.json crons, the x-vercel-forwarded-for trust in lib/auth/rate-limit.ts); data, auth, file storage, realtime, secrets and scheduled jobs run on hosted Supabase. Hosts from public/openapi.json: local http://localhost:3000, staging https://staging-upexbunkai.vercel.app, production https://upexbunkai.vercel.app.

Request and data flow

  1. middleware.ts builds a Supabase server client and calls auth.getUser(), which refreshes the session cookie.
  2. Under a protected prefix (/home /projects /onboarding /settings /activity /atcs /workspaces) with no user, it redirects 302 to /login?next=…. /api/v1 is not gated by middleware.
  3. Pages are Server Components that read through the cookie client, so RLS applies as the user.
  4. API routes go through withApiHandler (lib/api/handler.ts). Each route declares one posture: public, cookie-only, authenticated or required with a capability list; a posture scanner test enforces that none is missing.
  5. The gateway resolves the principal: a Bearer PAT first, otherwise the cookie session. principal.db is an RLS-scoped client in both cases.
  6. Data access is .from() or .rpc('bunkai_*') against Postgres, where RLS policies and SECURITY DEFINER RPCs enforce the rules. Errors come back in one ApiError envelope with x-request-id.

The service-role client (lib/supabase/admin.ts) bypasses RLS. It is used for the idempotency store, PAT lookup, the auth endpoints, the Stripe webhook, admin cron routes, invites, imports, token minting, export and the Jira and billing runners. 77 route files import it; spot checks show most use it only for idempotency keys while data stays on principal.db, but not every route was reviewed (see gaps).

Auth flow

  1. The login page is email-first: the UI calls POST /api/v1/auth/check-email (rate limited), which answers whether the account exists and is confirmed.
  2. Password sign-in goes to Supabase Auth; @supabase/ssr writes the session into sb-<project-ref>-auth-token cookies. A separate bk_active_ws cookie holds the active workspace.
  3. Sign-up (POST /api/v1/auth/signup, password 8 to 128 characters) requires a 6-digit emailed OTP (POST /api/v1/auth/confirm, resend via /auth/resend).
  4. Magic link (POST /api/v1/auth/magic-link) is login-only, it never creates a user.
  5. OAuth with GitHub or Google uses PKCE plus a bkstate CSRF cookie; callback at app/auth/callback/route.ts.
  6. Headless: POST /api/v1/auth/signin takes email and password and returns a session plus a freshly minted PAT, with no email step for a confirmed account.
  7. PAT calls send Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_<prefix>.<secret>. The gateway looks the token up by prefix, compares a SHA-256 hash kept in access_token_secrets, checks revocation and expiry, then mints a 60-second HS256 user JWT so RLS sees the token owner. Any failure is a uniform 401.

Authorization: workspace roles viewer, member, admin, owner (0001_tenancy.sql), checked in SQL by bunkai_is_workspace_member, bunkai_can_write_workspace, bunkai_is_workspace_admin, bunkai_is_workspace_owner (0005_rls_helpers.sql). PAT scopes are atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin (lib/api/capabilities.ts); workspace:admin cannot be minted headlessly, and token issuance is cookie-only (a PAT cannot mint a PAT).

What resists automation: sign-up and magic link need mailbox access; OAuth needs real GitHub or Google accounts. No captcha exists. Tests should start from a pre-provisioned confirmed account and use /auth/signin or a PAT (see ADR-0027).

Database

Hosted Supabase Postgres, reached through supabase-js / PostgREST and 130 bunkai_* RPCs (typed in lib/supabase/rpc.ts, generated types in lib/types/supabase.ts). RLS is on across the schema (about 153 policies); workspace_jira_connections has RLS with no client policy, so only the service role reads it. Extensions: pgcrypto, pg_cron, supabase_vault.

Subsystems: tenancy and invites, authoring (projects, modules, stories, acceptance criteria, ATCs, tests), execution (runs, steps, evidence, automated runs), defects, reporting (coverage, traceability, metrics), planning (test plans, milestones, environments), collaboration (chat, notifications, activity, saved views), billing, integrations (Jira), auth rate limit, idempotency, workspace export and deletion. Tables, columns and lifecycles belong to business-data-context (bun run context:map business-data-context), not yet generated.

Background work: pg_cron sweeps abandoned runs every 15 minutes (0075), inactive agent runs every 5 minutes (0122), rate-limit hits hourly (0103), and purges soft-deleted workspaces daily at 03:00 (0084). Vercel crons call /api/v1/admin/send-digest at 08:00 and /api/v1/admin/storage-cleanup at 03:00. Storage buckets run-evidence and workspace-exports are private. Realtime publishes run_atcs, run_steps, notifications and chat_messages.

QA database access: migration 0085 creates qa_inspector_ro and qa_inspector_rw roles; scripts/provision-qa-roles.ts sets their passwords, and the connection strings are the env names QA_INSPECTOR_RO_URL / QA_INSPECTOR_RW_URL.

QA relevance

  • The API gateway is the cheapest place to test business rules: every rule is reachable through /api/v1 with a PAT, and cookie and PAT behave the same by design (lib/api/rls-parity.test.ts).
  • RLS and role checks live in SQL, so authorization tests need one user per role (viewer, member, admin, owner) in the same workspace.
  • Staging has no Vercel crons (they register only on production, per the BK-882 comment), so digest and cleanup cannot be observed there without calling the admin routes.
  • ADRs seeded by this phase: .context/ADR/ADR-0027-bunkai-auth-in-tests.md, .context/ADR/ADR-0028-bunkai-selector-contract.md (both Accepted).

Stripe: a missing key answers 503 payment_processor_unavailable; the webhook verifies the signature, deduplicates by event id through an RPC, and returns 200 {status:'ignored'} for events it does not handle. A failed payment opens a grace window with a retry route (billing/retry).

Resend: a missing or bad key fails the send and logs it per user, never at boot. The default sender is the Resend sandbox (onboarding@resend.dev), which only delivers to verified recipients.

Jira Cloud: the client backs off exponentially on 429 and raises JiraAuthError on auth failure; the site must match https://<name>.atlassian.net (SQLSTATE 45420).

The legacy .context/SRS/architecture-specs.md also names Cloudflare R2, Sentry and PostHog; none of them is in package.json or the source.

Backend

The backend is the Next.js route handlers under app/api/v1/ plus Postgres RPCs; it ships in the same repo and deployment as the frontend. Bun runs scripts and tests (bun.lock); the app runs as Vercel serverless functions. No engines, .nvmrc or .bun-version pins a version. No ORM: @supabase/supabase-js ^2.106 and @supabase/ssr ^0.10.3 with typed RPC wrappers (lib/supabase/rpc.ts). Path aliases @/*, @app/*, @components/*, @lib/*.

Commands (target package.json)

bun install
bun run dev              # next dev, http://localhost:3000
bun test                 # every colocated *.test.ts(x)
bun run types:check      # tsc --noEmit
bun run lint:check       # eslint .
bun run openapi:gen      # writes public/openapi.json
bun run openapi:check    # spec drift gate
bun run types:gen        # Supabase types
bun run db:qa-roles      # set qa_inspector_* passwords
bun run release:check    # release ledger gate

Project rule in the target (.agents/instructions/agent-project.md, NO-LOCAL-BUILD): never run bun run build locally, it clobbers .next/; builds happen on Vercel.

Tests in the target

  • 415 colocated *.test.ts(x) files run by bun test; DOM tests use happy-dom.
  • DB integration tests (*-isolation.test.ts, lib/auth/rate-limit.db.test.ts, route tests that sign in) need NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING, QA_E2E_USER_EMAIL, QA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD. Without them they skip with a warning, so a green run does not prove DB behaviour.
  • With env present they run against the real shared database and clean up their own fixtures.
  • RUN_EMAIL_AUTH_TESTS=1 opts in to tests that send real signup email through the shared Resend account (a plain run once burned the quota).

Database and migrations

  • 122 files supabase/migrations/NNNN_<slug>.sql, applied to the remote project with the Supabase MCP apply_migration (writes the ledger row); never DDL through execute_sql.
  • No supabase/config.toml, no local Supabase stack, no seed data. QA accounts and workspaces are created through the API.
  • Migrations are applied once the PR review is approved, before merge, so staging code and schema stay in step. No down-migrations exist.
  • QA DB roles qa_inspector_ro (SELECT) and qa_inspector_rw (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE), both BYPASSRLS and both denied the three secret tables (access_token_secrets, magic_link_token_secrets, workspace_invite_secrets). Reached through the Supabase Session Pooler on port 5432 (not 6543), user form <DBHUB_USER>.<project-ref>, via the dbhub MCP and its DBHUB_* variables.
  • Because the QA roles bypass RLS, tenant isolation must be probed with a real user session: log in as user B, query user A's workspace, expect zero rows.
  • bunkai_sweep_abandoned_runs is not workspace-scoped: calling it from a test aborts inactive runs for every tenant.

Local-dev recipe

  1. bun install (runs husky setup).
  2. Build .env with the names in the table above; values come from the credentials Epic, never from chat or git.
  3. No local migration step: the remote project already holds 0001 to 0123.
  4. bun run dev, then GET /api/v1/health returns {ok, service, env, ts} (env from VERCEL_ENV, local when unset).

Auth request contract

POST /api/v1/auth/signin (public, app/api/v1/auth/signin/route.ts):

FieldRule
emailrequired, email, max 254
passwordrequired, 6 to 128 (sign-up enforces 8; 6 kept for legacy passwords)
pat_nameoptional, 1 to 80, default cli-signin
pat_scopesoptional, defaults atc:read, atc:write, run:execute; workspace:admin returns 403
pat_expires_in_daysoptional, 1 to 365, default no expiry

200 returns user, session (access and refresh token), pat (bk_pat_…, shown once) and sets the Supabase session cookies on the response. 401 is a uniform "Invalid email or password." (also for an unconfirmed account), 422 on validation, 400 on invalid JSON. Of the API handlers, four are cookie-only and answer 403 to a PAT: POST /api/v1/tokens, DELETE /api/v1/tokens/{id}, POST /api/v1/me/active-workspace, DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/membership (from the /qa page).

Shared database. Local, staging and "production" read and write the same Supabase project; the target says it holds no real customer data and a clean production project replaces it at the official release. Data a QA session creates on staging is visible everywhere, and pg_cron jobs (run sweeps, rate-limit purge, workspace purge) run regardless of environment.

Auth configuration (email templates, OTP length and expiry, SMTP, redirect allow-list, rate limits) lives only in the Supabase dashboard and is shared by all environments; site_url is pinned to http://localhost:3000 and the auth email rate limit is 30 per hour (.context/release/pending-production-v2.md). Auth OTP mail comes from no-reply@mail.upexgalaxy.com; the digest uses the Resend sandbox sender.

Monitoring and rollback

Monitoring is the JSON access log on stdout, indexed by Vercel, plus x-request-id; no error tracking. No rollback runbook: app rollback would be a Vercel redeploy of a previous build; the database has no down-migrations. Hotfix process: branch off main, PR to main, back-merge into staging the same day.

CI/CD

There is no CI pipeline: no .github/, no other CI config, no Dockerfile or IaC. Vercel builds on push through its Git integration (inferred; not configured in the repo).

StageWhat runsFound in
pre-commitlint-staged (eslint, prettier), types:check, vars:check, skills:check, conditional framework gates, openapi:check when spec sources change.husky/pre-commit, .husky/framework-gates.sh
pre-pushformat:check, lint:check, vars:env:check (warn), registry, compat and docs checks, openapi-gen --check. No bun test.husky/pre-push
commit-msgforensic trailer check, warn-only.husky/commit-msg

Release gatebun run release:check over the release ledger (.context/release/pending-production-v<N>.md), before promoting staging to main.context/release/README.md

Branch flow (target strategy main-integration): feature branches from staging, merged back with a merge commit; release is a fast-forward of main to staging; main and staging are protected.

QA relevance: nothing runs the 415 unit and DB tests automatically, so the Playwright suite in this repo, run from CI here, would be the only automated gate. A release can be watched by checking the open entries of the current release ledger.

Discovery gaps

  • No CI/CD definition in the target repo: Vercel Git integration, preview-per-PR behaviour and required checks on the GitHub ruleset are unverifiable from code (check the Vercel and GitHub dashboards).
  • Credentials Epic BK-29 exists on the current Jira site (checked in Phase 4); the /qa page still links it on the older host jira.upexgalaxy.com.
  • The /qa page lists one demo identity (a QA bot) and no per-role accounts; ADR-0027 needs one confirmed account per workspace role.
  • OTP length: the /qa page says 6 to 8 digits, the release ledger says 8 and was not yet observed in delivered mail.
  • Production domain: the target config mentions bunkai.io "post-MVP"; whether it is live is unknown.
  • Stripe test vs live keys per Vercel environment.
  • Handler count: /qa says about 92 handlers, the route tree has about 130 route.ts files and the spec 110 paths; not reconciled.
